newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sometime rival Singapore optimistic on Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Sometime rival Singapore optimistic on Hong Kong.

text.p: Singapore, often viewed as a rival of Hong Kong for investment and business, said on Friday it was confident the British colony would thrive after its handover to China next week.
Hong Kong reverts to China at midnight on Monday, June 30 after 156 years under British rule.
"Singapore is confident that Hong Kong will thrive under the principle of 'one country, two systems'," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement.

Saying Singapore and Hong Kong have always enjoyed good relations, the statement adds: "Singapore looks forward to further deepening and widening of her close relationship with the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR)."
China has said it will treat Hong Kong as an SAR with a large degree of autonomy, although critics question Beijing's commitment to human rights and democracy in the territory.
Singapore, like Hong Kong largely made up of ethnic Chinese, was also once under British rule.
It has been a fully independent state since the breakup in 1965 of a brief union with Malaysia.
